clue.text: Label these clothes? That's not a job for Miss Worthington

definitions.text: That's not a job for Miss Worthington
definitions.note: a career Noel Coward warned against

indicators.note: to clothe is to wrap or cover, so the word these is dressed around the label

parts.note: taken as written
a tag is a label attached to something

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to put name labels on garments, and is told this is not work for a certain young lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb: THESE wraps round TAG. Noel Coward's song runs 'Don't put your daughter on the stage, Mrs Worthington', so her daughter, Miss Worthington, is kept from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward's famous song warns the mother against letting her daughter pursue an acting career in the theatre.

clue.text: Film featuring sailor, unknown soldier, ambassador and primate stuck on island

indicators.note: stuck on means attached, so the last piece joins the rest

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Z is a mathematical unknown
a soldier is a type of ant
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
an ape is a primate
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A film cast: a sailor, a mystery soldier, an envoy and a monkey marooned together.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland; ambassadors are addressed as His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan the Ape Man is the 1932 jungle adventure starring Johnny Weissmuller.

clue.text: Filled with malice, the first lady holds tail of Tasmanian devil up

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a demon is a devil

explanation.surface: A spiteful First Lady holds a Tasmanian devil up by the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first lady' is not a president's wife but Eve; 'up' reverses DEMON in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Envenomed literally means poisoned, and figuratively embittered or full of spite.

clue.text: Leaks telephone call to The Sun

parts.note: a tinkle is British slang for a phone call, as in 'give me a tinkle'
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: Someone leaks a story by phoning The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaks' looks like press leaks, but means urinates.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinkle is a childish informal word for urinating, and a leak is slang for the same.

clue.text: "You rang" said Lurch, not ultimately happy, to Mr and Mrs Addams?

indicators.note: to lurch is to stagger about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: you is written U in text shorthand

explanation.surface: The gloomy butler Lurch answers his employers in The Addams Family with his catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lurch' is both the butler and the anagram signal for U plus RANG SAID. The phrase 'not ultimately happy' has no clear role in this parse: it may describe Lurch's mood only.
explanation.definitionFit: Gomez and Morticia are parents with legal care of Wednesday and Pugsley, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Character actor

definitions.meaning: a ... is the distinctive nature or mark of something, as in 'a man of that ...'
Terence ... is an English film actor

explanation.surface: A two-word description of a type of performer who plays quirky supporting roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character actor' reads as one phrase, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp means distinctive quality or kind, and Terence Stamp is a well-known British screen performer.

clue.text: Advances, first to last

parts.note: subs are advances of money against pay
first is written 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An instruction to move the first item to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' looks like a letter-moving instruction; 'to last' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsist is to continue existing or keep going, so it means endure.

clue.text: Old programmer goes to gym to get fit

parts.note: Ada Lovelace is regarded as the first computer programmer
PT, physical training, is school gym

explanation.surface: A retired coder heads to the gym to get into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is a verb meaning adjust, not healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to make it suitable or adjust it for a purpose.

clue.text: Restore mouldy pie with spice and ketchup

indicators.note: mouldy suggests rotten and broken down, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Rescuing a mouldy pie with spices and ketchup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouldy' rearranges the letters of PIE, SPICE and KETCHUP.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means put things back in order after a disaster.

clue.text: Women avoiding regular payments for years

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: wages are regular payments for work

explanation.surface: Women have gone without their regular pay for years.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages informally means a very long time, many years.

clue.text: Chicken decapitated crow

indicators.note: beheading a word removes its first letter, here the opening C

parts.note: chicken as an adjective means cowardly, which is craven

explanation.surface: A beheaded chicken lies beside a crow, like a grisly farmyard scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like the bird, but means cowardly: CRAVEN, which loses its head to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is the largest member of the crow family of black birds.

clue.text: Gaelic eccentric receives a pair of cups relating to mathematical work

indicators.note: one piece takes another into its middle, as a receiver holds what it is given
something eccentric is off-centre or odd, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a bra has two cups

explanation.surface: An odd Gael is handed two trophies for some mathematical achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' turns GAELIC into ALGEIC, which 'receives' BRA after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics, and the adjective describes anything belonging to it.

clue.text: Bin Laden trained missing book worm

indicators.note: trained suggests drilled into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
missing tells us a piece is taken away from the name

explanation.surface: A notorious terrorist was schooled without any book, a worm of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing book' drops B from BINLADEN, and 'trained' rearranges the remaining INLADEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelids are segmented worms, the group including earthworms and leeches.

clue.text: Mum's institute occasionally has tissue massage

parts.note: mum as in 'keep mum' means be quiet, which is sh

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A mother's organisation sometimes offers tissue massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother but the call for silence, SH; 'occasionally' takes the even letters of 'has tissue' for ATSU.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese therapy applying finger pressure to points on the body.

clue.text: Maybe pot's the last thing you'll need during meditation

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: TM stands for Transcendental Meditation

indicators.note: the last thing of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A pot of tea may be the last thing you'll want while meditating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe pot' signals an example; the final letter of 'you' goes inside TM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a protruding belly, and tum is the informal word for stomach.

clue.text: What an alligator may do to recover quickly

definitions.meaning: an alligator might snap its jaws out of the water at something
to come round sharply from a mood or daze

explanation.surface: A wildlife fact about how an alligator heals fast.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator snapping its jaws out of the water is the literal reading; the idiom means to shake off a mood or daze abruptly.

clue.text: Subdued individual catches part of speech given to troops

indicators.note: catches means holds, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: given to means added to, joining the two pieces

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A shy person overhears a speech delivered to the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of speech' is a grammar term, VERB, not a portion of an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Overborne means overpowered or overcome, so a subdued person has been overwhelmed.

clue.text: Anna Friel's drunk the wine of Pontius Pilate

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering and muddled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Actress Anna Friel has drunk the governor of Judea's wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a verb with Anna Friel as its subject; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Falernian was a prized ancient Roman vintage, so a Roman governor like Pilate might have drunk it.

clue.text: Aims to install new lenses and start to see infinity

indicators.note: installing puts something inside, so the other pieces go within the aims

parts.note: aims and ends are both goals

indicators.note: new letters made from old ones signal a rearrangement
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An optician's purpose: fitting fresh lenses so a patient can begin to see forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns LENSES into LESSNE; with S from 'start to see' this goes inside ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinity is the state of being without limit or conclusion, which is what the abstract noun expresses.

clue.text: Model who unloaded recycled timber

indicators.note: recycled means remade, so the letters are rearranged
unloaded means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A model who emptied her truck of recycled timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unloaded' empties WHO to WO; 'recycled' mixes MODEL with WO.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmwood is the timber of the elm tree.

clue.text: German-English painter, getting worse over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: worse in health means sicker

explanation.surface: A German-born English artist growing more ill as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Sickert was born in Munich and worked in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was a Munich-born British Impressionist artist of the Camden Town Group.

clue.text: Stretcher carrying Salieri? The opposite

indicators.note: carrying would put a word inside another, here that container is the composer's name
the opposite says to swap the roles, so the name holds the answer rather than being held

explanation.surface: A medic's stretcher bears the composer Salieri, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the answer would carry SALIERI; 'The opposite' says SALIERI carries it. 'Stretcher' is slang for a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is an old informal word for an exaggeration or untruth.

clue.text: Rolling agenda, involving Mike Pence, makes one wonder

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so one piece holds another
rolling suggests turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a diary is a book of engagements, like an agenda
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An agenda that keeps changing, featuring US politician Mike Pence, is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike Pence' looks like the vice-president, but gives M and P. 'Rolling' turns DIARY into YRAID, which holds M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Pyramid of Giza is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

clue.text: Put up beams in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Stage lighting beams are installed in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift or erect it.

clue.text: Mythical queen languished, devoid of ecstasy and love

indicators.note: devoid of means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: languished can mean wasted away and died
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A legendary queen pined, lacking joy and love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstasy' is not joy but the drug, E; 'love' is the tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido, Queen of Carthage, killed herself when Aeneas left her in Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Rum barrels in front of top-class drinking club?

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
a club is one of the four card suits, so a card

explanation.surface: Barrels of rum stand outside a smart drinking club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' is the definition, not an adjective; B from 'barrels' leads AI with CARD inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a famous brand of rum originally from Cuba.

clue.text: A way to purchase flexible armour by post?

definitions.text: A way to purchase flexible armour by post?

parts.words: A way to purchase flexible armour by post?
parts.note: chain mail is flexible armour, so ordering it through the post would be buying by catalogue and delivery

explanation.surface: A question about how a knight might buy chain mail remotely.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying goods from a catalogue and receiving them by post is the usual meaning, and here the goods are chain armour too.

clue.text: Drug company dumped retrograde computer

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is reversed
dumped means thrown out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: cocaine is a drug

explanation.surface: A drug firm scrapped an old-fashioned computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumped' takes CO from COCAINE, leaving CAINE, which 'retrograde' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: ENIAC was among the first general-purpose electronic digital machines, built in the USA in the 1940s.

clue.text: A legion will get turned on and climax

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: a climax is the end point of something

explanation.surface: A Roman legion is excited and reaches a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ON. 'A legion' means a great many, used as an adverbial phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very much or a huge number, just as a legion is a vast multitude.

clue.text: Punishments by educators and teachers is niggling grammar schools' principals

indicators.note: principals are heads, so take the head letter of each word

parts.words: by educators and teachers is niggling grammar schools'

explanation.surface: Corporal punishments by teachers bother the heads of grammar schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principals' plays on school heads; it means the first letters of the eight words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashings administered as discipline were once common corporal punishments in schools.
